label: Area Line Chart
title: Area Line Chart
summary: Show a continuous trend and make series comparison legible.
corePrinciple: Make direction and comparison legible before detail.

anatomy.title: Direction, comparison, and detail have distinct jobs
anatomy.description: The chart combines axes, a plotted series, optional dots, a legend for comparison, and a goal pin when a target matters.
blocks: Use one unit and a readable scale so the direction is honest.
Area and line show the trend; projected points use the dashed treatment. The plot owns pointer and x-axis selection.
Use a goal pin to call out a meaningful point, not a decorative maximum.
Keep labels short enough to select and read at the host width.

sizing.title: Give the plot enough width for its labels
sizing.description: The chart owns plot height while the host supplies width. On a narrow host, use shorter labels and fewer points in the same order.
blocks: Select an x-axis point to inspect its values.

content.title: Make units and series names do the reading work
content.description: Short x labels, one shared unit, and a visible legend help the chart communicate before a person inspects a point.
blocks: Use the same unit and scale for series that people need to compare.

A legend removes ambiguity when lines overlap or cross.
Keep the visible values available in text when SVG interaction is not enough for the task.

sources.title: Grounded in the public chart contract
sources.description: This guide uses the published AreaLineChart API, the inspected Figma master, and the canonical Storybook stories.
blocks: Default, overlap, forecast, and interactive stories

Examples use public AreaLineChart and its public interaction model from jfs-components 0.1.78. The Y-axis column reserves the width of its widest tick label, and the goal pin stays inside the plot. The chart derives a nice tick domain from its data unless y bounds are supplied, and its plot height excludes the x-axis row. Projected points, selected indices, goal pins, curves, grid, dots, and legends are public choices. SVG interaction is keyboard reachable through the public x-axis Pressable in RN Web, but the rendered accessibility tree does not expose full series labels; the guide keeps a visible values table.
